_comment: Wyoming 2027 Affordable Housing Allocation Plan (HOME, NHTF, 4% and 9% LIHTC), Wyoming Community Development Authority. The document states no cycle beyond its title year; cycle is left to data/sources.csv. Page numbers are PDF page indices; the printed number matches up to p.19 and runs one lower from PDF p.20, where printed page 19 repeats. Scoring Allocation Criteria, PDF pp.37-50. The summary table on pp.37-38 lays out a Negative and a Maximum Points column that the text layer interleaves; it was read from the rendered page images. It states 'TOTALS -1510 495'. Hand-summed before loading from the section subtotals: 158 + 65 + 77 + 85 + 40 + 70 = 495, which the loader matched. The negatives reconcile too: -30 in Housing Needs (carried inside 1.d and 1.e, which score in both directions), -280 in Project Location (-30 dynamic, -50 concentration, -200 environmental) and -1200 in Financials (-200 subsidy, -1000 costs) make -1510. Three internal contradictions are recorded: the Housing Needs header says 'up to negative 28 points' against -30 in its parts; the Project Location header says 'Up to a negative 250 points' against -280 in the summary; and the Donations example awards 35 points for a 10% contribution that its own 3-points-per-1% rule values at 30. Thresholds are in WY_thresholds.json.

track_totals.note: Summary table, pp.37-38: 'TOTALS -1510 495', read from the rendered pages because the text layer interleaves the Negative and Maximum Points columns. 495 is the sum of the six section subtotals (158, 65, 77, 85, 40, 70). Negative points are excluded, as everywhere in the corpus; the -1510 is recorded in the notes of the negative criteria. The Housing Needs category must reach 100 of its 158 for an application to be scored.

criteria.heading: Income levels (market study capture rate)
criteria.note: The lower the market study's capture rate, the more points: 28 at 5% or below, falling by 2 per 5 points of capture rate to 0 above 70%. The Housing Needs category needs at least 100 of its 158 points for the application to be scored at all.

criteria.heading: Saturation
criteria.note: 48 minus the saturation percentage (proposed units / income-restricted units needed) as a whole number; the document's example is 13% saturation earning 35. Fully occupied or waitlisted rehab projects get the maximum.

criteria.heading: Absorption rate
criteria.note: Fully occupied or waitlisted rehab projects get the maximum.

criteria.heading: Vacancy in community
criteria.quote: Vacancy in Community (Maximum 40 points; up to negative 20 points)
criteria.note: Two ladders that add, market study (up to 25) and the state vacancy survey (up to 15), for 40. Each ladder runs on below zero: 0 at 8.01-10%, -5 at 10.01-12% and -10 above 12%, which is where the 'up to negative 20 points' comes from. Recorded as one criterion scoring in both directions (the Virginia pattern), with the negative rows described here rather than tiered.

criteria.heading: Vacancy in low-income projects
criteria.quote: Vacancy in Low-Income Projects (Maximum 28 points; up to negative 10 points)
criteria.note: Continues below zero: -5 at 6.01-8% and -10 at 8.01-10%. Projects in communities with over 10% vacancy in income-restricted projects are not considered unless they are rehabilitations with under 10% vacancy themselves. CONTRADICTION: the Housing Needs header on p.39 says 'up to negative 28 points', but its two components carry -20 and -10, and the summary table on p.37 gives -30.

criteria.heading: Construction/energy efficiency standards exceeded

tiers.tier_label: Energy Star refrigerator, dishwasher, ceiling fans and washer/dryer

criteria.note: The items sum to exactly 65. Ceiling fans appear both inside the Energy Star appliance item and as their own 5-point item. Applicants may also 'advocate for points' for standards not listed, which leaves the test open-ended within the 65.

criteria.heading: Geographic distribution

tiers.tier_label: 2022 or earlier within the four-year look-back

criteria.note: Years since the community's last 9% award, within a four-year look-back. See 3.a.dynamic for the deduction applied when several applications come from one community.

criteria.heading: Dynamic scoring deduction for multiple applications in one community
criteria.quote: Dynamic Scoring: In the event that multiple applications are received
criteria.note: After final scoring: -10 for the second-highest application from the same community, -20 for the third, -30 for the fourth or lower. Depends entirely on the other applications.

criteria.heading: Proximity to services

tiers.tier_label: Recreation center or park within 1 mile

criteria.note: A distance matrix: grocery and retail pay 3, 4 and 5 at 2, 1.5 and 1 mile, the others 1, 2 and 3. The tiers give the 1-mile values; family projects count the school and senior projects the senior center, so either reaches 22. Communities lacking a service are scored case by case.

criteria.heading: Concentration of low-income housing
criteria.quote: Concentration of Low-Income Housing (Up to a negative 50 points)
criteria.note: At WCDA's judgement from visual observation, market study data and HUD CPD maps. Rehabilitation projects are exempt.

criteria.heading: Environmental: clean Phase I
criteria.quote: Environmental Items/Inappropriate Location (Maximum of 5 points; Up to a Negative 200 points)
criteria.note: Five points for a Phase I with no recognized environmental conditions or areas of concern; rehabilitation projects get the maximum. The same heading carries the -200 recorded in 3.d.neg.

criteria.heading: Environmental: unaddressed mitigation or inappropriate location
criteria.quote: Negative points will be assessed if the project will need mitigation that has not
criteria.note: Up to -200 for mitigation not addressed or budgeted under HUD Part 58, or a site in or near heavy industrial or commercial areas, containing hazardous materials, or otherwise unfit for housing. CONTRADICTION: the Project Location header (p.43) says 'Up to a negative 250 points', while the summary table (p.37) gives -280, which is -30 dynamic scoring plus -50 concentration plus -200 here.

criteria.heading: Community revitalization in QCT or revitalization plan
criteria.quote: Community Revitalization in Qualified Census Tracts And/or Community

tiers.tier_label: Existing housing used in a Community Revitalization Plan, or a jurisdiction actively reducing barriers
Tribal land, with the most recent Indian Housing Plan

criteria.note: The QCT and plan items add to 10; the tribal route reaches 10 alone. Generic community-wide housing studies are expressly not enough.

criteria.heading: Project and unit amenities

tiers.tier_label: Community laundry room on-site, new construction

criteria.note: The thirteen rows sum to exactly the stated 50, but only by counting both laundry rows, one for new construction (1) and one for acquisition/rehab (5). A project that is only one or the other tops out at 45 or 49. Coded at the stated 50 because a project with both components could arguably claim both; the reviewer should confirm.

tiers.tier_label: Option to buy, or WCDA-approved 99+ year lease before application
Zoning in place, no approval required
Zoning in place, other approvals required

criteria.heading: Projects with project-based rental assistance
criteria.quote: Projects with Project Based Rental Assistance (Maximum 15 points)

tiers.tier_label: Rehabilitation of an existing project with PBRA

criteria.heading: Property management team
criteria.note: Discretionary: WCDA's annual view of end-of-year reporting, financial assessment, risk management and monitoring findings. No scale is published.

criteria.heading: Development team
criteria.note: Discretionary: cost management, returned credits, timely completion, reporting, experience and communication. Developers new to Wyoming are scored on references from two other states. No scale is published.

criteria.heading: Loan terms (HOME and NHTF requests)
criteria.note: The larger the HOME or NHTF request, the more points; the HOME ladder (up to 20) and NHTF ladder (up to 15) add to 35. A LIHTC-only application scores nothing here. As written, requests of exactly $1,000,000 or $750,000 fall between rows.

criteria.heading: Subsidy above per-unit limits
criteria.note: -10 per 1% over the Attachment A per-unit eligible basis or subsidy limits.

criteria.heading: Donations, grants and waived fees
criteria.note: CONTRADICTION, recorded not resolved: the rule is '3 points per 1% in waivers and/or contributions', which reaches 35 at about 11.7% of project costs, but the document's own example gives a 10% reduction 35 points, where the rule gives 30. Non-federal contributions from unrelated parties only; deferred developer fee does not count.

criteria.heading: Total project costs above limits
criteria.quote: Total Project Costs (Up to a negative 1000 points)
criteria.note: -10 per 1% over the Attachment A total project cost limits, up to -1000: large enough to eliminate any application. WCDA may waive all negative points for one over-limit project a round and offer a pro-rated award under the Statistical Outlier Method (p.50).

criteria.heading: Rehabilitation with project-based rental assistance
criteria.quote: Rehabilitation Proposal with Project Based Rental Assistance

criteria.heading: Rehabilitation without project-based rental assistance
criteria.quote: Rehabilitation Proposal without Project Based Rental Assistance
